stories.headline: RUSSIA FIRES 400 DRONES AND 110 MISSILES AT UKRAINE, AND SOME CROSS INTO POLAND
stories.summary: One of the largest combined strikes of the war hit bridges and energy facilities around Kyiv, killing at least eight people. Polish and allied aircraft were scrambled as missiles briefly entered Polish airspace, turning a national attack into a test of NATO air defence on the alliance's eastern edge.

stories.headline: TRUMP MEETS XI AND PUTIN, THEN THREATENS TO BLOCK US FIRMS FROM BUILDING DATA CENTRES ABROAD
stories.summary: In his first public remarks since returning from Asia, the US president said companies would either be barred from building data centres overseas or face a heavy tax, linking the AI boom directly to national policy.

stories.headline: TRUMP OPEN TO GIVING KYIV A NATO-LIKE MUTUAL DEFENCE GUARANTEE
stories.summary: Envoy Jared Kushner said the president is open to extending Ukraine a security commitment resembling NATO's mutual defence clause, while stressing that details were still being negotiated.

stories.headline: SENATE REJECTS WAR POWERS RESOLUTION AS THE IRAN CONFLICT ESCALATES AGAIN
stories.summary: The Senate voted down an attempt to limit the president's authority to strike Iran. Trump said he is in no rush to decide on further military action and would wait until the new year, even as fighting quietly intensified this week and war funding threatened a government shutdown fight.

stories.headline: THOUSANDS PROTEST IN MORE THAN 25 COUNTRIES OVER WAGES AND PUBLIC SERVICES
stories.summary: Demonstrations began on Friday across over 25 European countries and were expected to continue through the weekend, with unions demanding higher pay and restored public spending.

stories.headline: WAR FUNDING FIGHT PUTS THE US GOVERNMENT ON SHUTDOWN WATCH
stories.summary: A dispute over funding for the Iran war moved to the centre of budget talks in Washington, raising the prospect of a lapse in federal funding.
